The chair urged that parks budget money not be left to revert to the general fund at year end, since lack of upkeep spending caused the current facility problems.
The town recently received nearly two hundred thousand dollars for engineering for the park.
Both commission capital requests rank mid-pack; the remaining request total dropped after the engineering was funded, and the weeds project may be retitled to include Marshall Pond.
Reimbursed grant money returns to free cash and would need town meeting to be reallocated, and it is unclear whether that satisfies the ARPA use deadline.
The town manager prefers going to town meeting once, but members accepted going twice because the large grants arrive at different times.
The commission compared its per-player fees with school hourly rates and discussed hourly versus flat or seasonal fees for adult groups, the Phillies and other users; no change was made.

Marshall Park design IFB draft: members agreed to help, with the chair to take a first pass over the holidays and share it for member input.
Karen will contact the land and water conservation grant staff to ask if the project is ready to apply before starting the application due in late January.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted by roll call, three ayes, to have the chair ask the town manager to install sidewalks from the rotary to the town beach, if town funds are available.
Members spent the longest stretch of the meeting on 2023 field and user fees and made no change, deferring specific proposals to the next meeting.
The Commission voted, three ayes, to accept the new McNally Park sign as a gift to the town.
Members supported paying for the town beach house repair from the parks revolving fund and accepted going to town meeting twice for Marshall Park funding.
The town manager is to seek a quote for the Powell field vandalism damage and consider an insurance claim, and a member will ask the police chief about cameras in parks.

why_it_matters: Field and user fees for groups such as Little League and adult leagues were discussed but left unchanged, so what residents' groups pay in 2023 is still undecided.

Beach house repairs would come from the parks revolving fund, which is mostly beach fees, and Marshall Park would need two town meeting votes for funding, so residents may be asked to vote on it more than once.
watch_next: Next meeting on January 18th, where members are to bring specific fee proposals and review possible storage and concession stand charges.
Late-January deadline for the land and water conservation grant application for Marshall Park.
